svg.text: Software architecture is the art of drawing lines (boundaries) that separate elements and restrict those on one side from knowing about those on the other; early lines
defer decisions and keep them from polluting the core business logic
GUI component
Database component
DatabaseAccess implements the interface
BusinessRules component
contains the DatabaseInterface
Web, console, SOA UIs
Oracle, MySQL, Couch, Datomic, flat
files
Draw lines between things that matter and things that do not
the GUI does not matter to the business rules, the database does not matter to the
GUI or the business rules. The business rules do not need the schema or query
language, only functions to fetch and save data, so put the database behind an
interface (Fig 17.1): the boundary crosses the inheritance relationship just below
DatabaseInterface (Fig 17.2) and the Database component depends on BusinessRules,
never the reverse (Fig 17.3)
Input and output are irrelevant
people mistake the GUI for the system; a video game's model could run without
drawing anything. The less relevant component depends on the more relevant one (Fig
17.4); plugins (Fig 17.5): the UI and database are plugins to the business rules,
replaceable (not always trivially: a client-server UI after a web one may rework
communication). ReSharper depends on Visual Studio's source, so JetBrains cannot
disturb Microsoft but Microsoft could disable ReSharper (Fig 17.6): the desirable
asymmetry
